question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x - y + z &=1 \\ 2 x - y + z &=3 \\ - x + y &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 2 z &=-56 \\ - 2 x + y - 3 z &=116 \\ 4 x - 3 y + 6 z &=-248\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 116 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -248\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 116 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -248\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 4 & -3 & 6 & -248\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -3 & -2 & -24\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -56 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -12\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -32 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -12\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-32 \\ y &=16 \\ z &=-12.\end{aligned}\right.

\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -9 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & -14 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 1 & -9 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -7 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a 3x3 System That Is Not in Row Echelon Form

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x + 3 y + 2 z &=-4 \\ x + 4 y + 2 z &=-1 \\ - 2 x - 6 y - 3 z &=9\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 1 & 4 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 1 & 4 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & -6 & -3 & 9\end{array}\right] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-2){R}_{3} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 0 & -6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & -15 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-15 \\ y &=3 \\ z &=1.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

So, we have the solution $x=-15$, $y=3$, and $z=1.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -15,3,1\rangle$.
